summary: This article explains why regular bathing, clean clothes, and trimmed nails, along with other everyday hygiene habits, help your body stay healthy.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “Keeping Clean: Hygiene and Health” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: very tiny living things; some are helpful and some can cause illness
an illness caused by germs getting into the body
a small amount of something left behind after most of it is gone

challengeTerms.def: the thin outer layer of the skin
a germ, such as a bacterium or virus, that can cause disease
a natural oil made by the skin

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that keeping your body clean is one of the most important things you can do to stay healthy? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Write a short guide for new students explaining why a daily hygiene routine matters and how to build one.
struggling: Pre-teach bacteria, infection, and residue with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use epidermis, pathogen, and sebum in a short paragraph that explains one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
